sentences: Orbit-finite automata recognize data words using infinitely many states organized into finitely many symmetry classes.
The project asks whether first-order definability of the recognized language can be decided.
The source conjectures that aperiodicity of the syntactic monoid provides the correct criterion within this automaton class.
Infinite-data languages outside the class show that aperiodicity alone is not a universal characterization.
Proving an effective criterion would extend a central connection between finite automata, algebra and logic to a controlled infinite-alphabet setting.
